title: Ryhti-hanke: Kulttuuriympäristön tietokomponenttikirjaston testaus
description: Hankinnan kohteena on Kulttuuriympäristön tietokomponenttikirjaston (tietomallin) sekä siihen liittyvien koodistojen testaaminen. Koodistot on linkattu tietomallin attribuutteihin. Testauksen menetelmä ja toteutustapa on toimittajan itse valittavissa ja se tulee esittää tarjouksen liitteenä toteutussuunnitelmassa. Työn tavoitteena on validoida tehtyjen tietomallissa määriteltyjen kulttuuriympäristön tietojen määrittelyjen laatua. Testauksen kautta varmistetaan, onko tietomallin attribuuteissa täydennettävää tai karsittavaa sekä ovatko siihen liittyvät koodistot riittävän kattavia. Tietomallimäärittelyjä testataan hyödyntämällä oikeita suojelupäätöksiä. Myös riittävät kytkökset kaava- ja rakennustietoihin sekä paikkatietojen samankaltaisuus on varmistettava. Tietomallia tulee testata eri kulttuuriympäristön työprosessien näkökulmasta. Tätä varten testiaineistona käytetään seuraavien tietojärjestelmien aineistoja: - ELY-keskukset: GISALU ja Access - Museovirasto: Rakennusperintörekisteri - Alueelliset vastuumuseot: MIP (Turku), Kioski (Kokkola) ja Collecte (Keski-Suomi) - Metsähallitus: PAVE - Kirkkohallitus: BASIS-järjestelmä Testausprojektia varten kustakin testiaineiston vastuutahosta on mukana projektissa henkilöitä. Tietojärjestelmien vastuutahot toimittavat sovitun määrän testiaineistoa sovitussa muodossa toimittajalle testausta varten. Testauksessa on otettava huomioon, että testiaineistona olevat oikeat suojelupäätökset sisältävät henkilötietoja (YM:n tietosuojaseloste). Lopputuloksena syntyy testauksen loppuraportti, jossa eritellään testauksen kautta löydetyt huomiot, välittömät korjaustarpeet sekä jatkokehitysehdotukset. Loppuraportissa eritellään ne testausaineiston tiedot, joille ei löydy vastaavuutta tietokomponenttikirjaston määrityksistä. Testauksen tuloksena olevissa johtopäätöksissä pitää käydä ilmi, aiheuttaako tietokomponenttikirjaston määritykset muutostarpeita testiaineistojen tietojärjestelmissä. Kulttuuriympäristön tietokomponenttikirjaston määrityksiä hyödynnetään tulevaisuudessa mahdollisen rakennetun ympäristön tietojärjestelmän kulttuuriympäristön tietovarannon määrittelyn pohjana. Projektin aluksi pidetään aloituskokous tilaajan ja tarjoajan välillä. Projektin päätteeksi pidetään loppupalaveri, jossa tarjoaja esittelee testauksen tulokset tilaajalle sekä tilaajan kutsumille sidosryhmille. Työssä tulee huomioida varahenkilöjärjestely mahdollisten esteiden varalle. Valittavan tarjoajan kanssa tehdään kirjallinen sopimus, jossa käytetään yleisinä sopimusehtoina JYSE 2014 (päivitys 2022) tavarat/palvelut -sopimusehtoja. Sopimusluonnos on tarjouspyynnön liitteenä.

title: AUTOMATED PHASED ARRAY FACTORY CALIBRATION FROM RADIATION PATTERN USING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (ARTES AT 7B.082) EXPRO+ RE-ISSUE
description: The objective of this activity is to develop automated factory calibration of phased arrays to improve the manufacturing process for satellite user terminals in the context of LEO constellations leveraging Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning techniquesTargeted Improvements: - Enable factory calibration (less than 1 second) from single-shot radiation pattern measurements of phased arrays. - Error between post-factory calibration theoretical should be below 0.5dBDescription:Traditionally, satellite manufacturing was focused on producing a limited number of bespoke satellites for GEO orbits. However, the rise of LEO constellations demandsa shift towards mass production, requiring efficient assembly and testing processes. This statement extends beyond satellite payloads to LEO user terminals, where phased arrays are becoming ubiquitous for constant asset tracking. With satellite user terminal systems increasingly reliant on phased arrays, precise calibration becomes crucial for optimal performance. Calibration involves ensuring precise alignment and amplitude matching of each element to achieve optimal beamforming, thereby maximising signal strength, and minimising interference. Still, current manual calibration methods are mostly labour-intensive, time-consuming, and prone to errors, presenting a challenge to the efficiency goals of mass manufacturing. To overcome this, there is a need to develop AI/ML solutions capable of extracting calibration insights from single-scan radiation patterns measurements. Previous research has demonstrated the potential of AI/ML techniques in synthesising radiation patterns, identifying faulty elements and predicting unmeasured phased values speeding up calibration of antenna arrays. Building upon these advancements, this activity will streamline the calibration process of phased arrays using AI/ML techniques. Rather than using brute force or iterative methods, the objective is to achieve fast calibration and accurate in a single shot. Additionally, the AI/ML engine will be capable to cope with process, voltage, and temperature variations inherent to the integrated circuits used in phased arrays, ensuring robust calibration across manufacturing batches. This approach not only addresses the immediate challenge of mass-producing user terminals but also lays the foundation for adaptabletesting systems capable of accommodating variations across manufacturing batches. By transitioning from labour-intensive manual methods to streamlined single-shot calibration, manufacturers can achieve greater efficiency and accuracy in production. The developed calibration process will be implemented in a combined software and hardware test-bed that will be developed, and the performance ofthe developed calibration process will be tested.

title: PROTOCOL STACK ENABLING VOICE-CALL USING NON-TERRESTRIAL IOT WAVEFORM (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 3F.013) - RE-ISSUE
description: The activity aims at the development of new functions in the protocol stack, in support of voice calls using the latest NTN NB-IoT waveform. The activity shall select the most promising voice encoder/decoder technology and shall demonstrate its fixability over a NB-IoT communication link via satellite..Targeted Improvements:Enrich the portfolio of satellite services supported with the NB-IoT technology.Description:With the endorsement of the Release 17 NTN NB-IoT specifications from the 3GPP community, new satellite services are recently announced based on this M2M/IoT technology. Currently, these services are intended only for short messaging and positioning information in the context of Machine-to-Machine (M2M) applications. On the other hand, relatively broadband type of services supported by the 5G NR standard is difficult to be initiated at the satellite L-/S- band, due to the limited capabilities of the current legacy systems and the need for dedicated non-geostationary satellite constellations. Looking at Voice-over-IP (VoIP) services, the latest AMR (Adaptive Multi-Rate) codec works with variable bit rates ranging from 4.75 to 12.2kbps, and with 20ms data arriving interval among the data packets. Consequently, it is of interest to evaluate the adoption of the NB-IoT standard to support voice calls in satellite networks. The activity shall therefore undertake the following steps: a) Review the latest 3GPP specifications for the NTN scenario (i.e., Release 18) and the identified solutions for satellite coverage enhancements; b) Given the current state-of-the-art AMR codec, design and develop the new functions in the protocol stack of both UE and gNB to support VoIP services for NGSO satellite networks; c) Thorough laboratory validation.

Anders als im Vorgängerprojekt „LOGIN“ (Lichtsignalanlagen optimal gesteuert im Nahverkehr), in welchem unter der Beteiligung von verschiedenen Forschungspartner ein Proof of Concept der C-ITS-basierten ÖV-Beschleunigung erbracht werden konnte, setzt C-Roads auf produktreife Hardware, die am Markt verfügbar ist. Zudem soll die Integration in das bestehende ITCS/Betriebsleitsystem der IVU Traffic Technologies AG (IVU) beispielweise für die Visualisierung von Schaltzeitprognosen erfolgen. Die ÜSTRA hat dazu Zuwendungen der European Climate, Infrastructure and Environment Executive Agency (CINEA) beantragt, die durch Zuwendungsbescheid vom 16. Oktober 2024 bewilligt wurden. Bewilligt wurde eine Anteilsfinanzierung. Die Inanspruchnahme der Zuwendungen wird von der ÜSTRA angestrebt. Daher erwartet die ÜSTRA eine termingerechte Fertigstellung der ausgeschriebenen Leistungen. Gegenstand der ausgeschriebenen Leistung ist die Lieferung und funktionsfähigen Bereitstellung einer fahrzeugseitigen C-ITS basierten ÖV-Beschleunigung, das sämtliche Leistungen für ein integriertes System beinhaltet. Hierzu gehören unter anderem die Lieferung und Installation von C-ITS OBUs, von Antennen als auch die Integration zwischen diesen Komponenten bis hin zur Schnittstelle zum ITCS-Bordrechner. Das anzubietende System soll als dauerhaft funktionierendes Gesamtsystem binnen 15 Monate nach Auftragserteilung implementiert und prüfbar abgerechnet werden. Durch den Einsatz einer C-ITS-basierten ÖV-Beschleunigung soll ein zukunftsfähiges und standardisiertes System umgesetzt werden, das flexibel und Hersteller unabhängig erweitert werden kann. Der Informationsaustausch mit der infrastrukturseitigen C-ITS Roadside Unit (RSU) muss nach den folgenden Standards erfolgen: • C-Roads Specification Release 3.2.0 C-ITS Message Profiles • ISO 3833 Vehicle Type • ETSI TS 103 301 V2.2.2 • OCA-MAPEM Region-ID-Registry 02-00-01 Die zu verwendenden C-ITS-Nachrichten für die Kommunikation zwischen C-ITS RSU und OBU sind folgend aufgelistet: • CAM • MAPEM • SPAT • SREM • SSEM

title: ESPRIT WIT Launch Vehicle Adapter (LVA)
description:
The Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a ‘basecamp’ for sustained lunar exploration. The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly. It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The Gateway – European System Providing Refueling Infrastructure and Telecommunication (ESPRIT) is ESA’s contribution of an infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with refueling, logistic and telecommunication functions (this latter function will be provided with a different element that will reach Gateway at a different time). The ESPRIT includes contributions from USA, and Canada. 
The ESPRIT WIT is the Windowed Infrastructure Tunnel devoted to the logistic and circular viewport functions, in addition to the Primary Structural function of the complete system.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for the development and qualification of the window panes coatings in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements” (reference ESA BEST PRACTICES IPC(2012)65, rev.2).

The Launch Vehicle Adapter (LVA) is a structural element, physically part of the ERM WIT Primary Structure, which shall ensure the fulfillment of the following main functions:

•	Provide the interface between the ERM WIT and the SLS adapter, adjusting the WIT diameter to the one of the Launcher adapter.
•	Provide the interface between the ERM WIT and the ERM UMAXT.

The LVA is a roll-forged truncated cone made of Titanium (Ti6Al4V), that shall be designed in order to guarantee both mechanical and thermal performances to meet the above functions.
Moreover its structure presents several holes in order to provide the piping and harness routing from the active IBDM to other services.

Further information concerning the ESPRIT campaign can be found on the Agency’s website here: https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Gateway_to_the_Moon. 
Notwithstanding the complete list of countries identified in the Special Provision for visibility purposes, the ITT letter of invitation will contain a dedicated set of geographical return requirements/targets to be considered.

title: EFFECTS OF THE SPATIO-TEMPORALLY VARYING ATMOSPHERE ON SAR IMAGING: THE IONOSPHERE CASE - EXPRO PLUS
description: To derive more accurate expression of atmosphere irregularities effects with a focus on the ionosphere, and devise mitigation techniques for both geo- and sun-synchronous SAR imaging systemsDescription: For Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) systems the atmospheric turbulence is generally assumed to be time-invariant during the synthetic aperture time due to itsshort duration. Such assumption is not always correct, as horizontal atmospheric drifts and vortices exist. Especially for SAR systems at low frequency (P-Band, L-Band), SAR operating on repeat-track basis, geo-synchronous SAR systems characterised by long integration time and extensive imaging scene, the ionosphere can have an important role on the performance. Furthermore, both temporal andspatial variations of the ionosphere have to be jointly taken into account, which further complicates their characterisation. Therefore, the effects of the flowing ionospheric irregularities need to be investigated, aiming in particular to image shifts, defocusing and repeat-track interferometry. The aim of this activity is to provide a comprehensive analysis to evaluate effects of both spatial variation and flowing ionospheric irregularities on SAR systems operating both at P-, L- and C-band. In particular, the ionospheric scintillations, which act remarkably in the polar cap and equatorial zone at night need to be considered. The Ionosphere characterisation shall originate from previous developments, analyses performed in the framework of previous missions developments and from knowledge built up in the navigation community. This activity encompasses the following tasks: -Analytical models of the physical effects of spatial-temporally ionospheric background variations on the SAR signal. - Assessment of the impacts on the SAR performancesdemonstrating, both theoretically and numerically, the geometric fidelity, focusing aspect and interferometry quality (i.e., relative image shifts and the decorrelation of interferometric pairs, interferometric phase screen errors). - Validation of the models andof the performance analysis using ionospheric monitoring measurements (i.e., Global Positioning System). - Develop mitigation techniques. - The implementation of the aforementioned components in a software framework. The methods developed in this activity are expected to be developed in such a way that they can be later broadened to other atmospheric effects such as tropospheric scintillations.
